issues.title: Logger v2
issues.sourceOfTruth: src/logger/structuredLogger.ts: LogRecord schema and grouping semantics
acceptance: LogRecord is the shared schema for extension, desktop, CLI, and tests.
Host packages define sinks/renderers only.
Legacy logUtils and AgentLogger paths are migrated or explicitly scheduled as temporary compatibility shims.

issues.title: CLI texra run
issues.sourceOfTruth: packages/cli/src/runtime/cliContext.ts for process data; packages/cli/src/runtime/exitCodes.ts for exit codes; shared executeAgent runtime for execution semantics
acceptance: texra run enters the shared executeAgent path.
CLI commands consume CliContext and do not read ambient process data.
Repository lint, typecheck, and CLI architecture guards include the CLI package.
The package build produces the manifest-declared binary.
The packaged binary path is validated for text, JSON, and NDJSON output.

issues.title: CLI approval policy
acceptance: The approval policy matrix is implemented for edit, bash, plan, proposal, retry, and external inquiry gates.
never and headless ask fail closed.
Shared coordinators own request identity and lifecycle.
Interactive ask prompts are serialized per CLI context.

issues.title: CLI texra chat
issues.sourceOfTruth: shared tool-use session lifecycle owns conversation semantics; CLI chat owns terminal input and presentation
acceptance: Chat rejects headless mode.
Chat provides user input and follow-up turns in the same tool-use session.
Terminal renderer is lazy-loaded from the chat path only.
OpenTUI is used only after Node 20+/npm distribution proof, otherwise a Node-stable renderer is used behind the same boundary.
Chat provides grouped, minimal, and hidden tool-display modes.
Chat provides a plain fallback input mode for conservative terminals.
Chat displays session metadata: active agent, active model, working directory, usage/cost when available, and resume identity.
Chat integrates permission prompts through the CLI approval adapter rather than duplicating approval lifecycle.
issues.partialDelivery: PR #3846 delivers the plain fallback input mode and shared follow-up path. Rich renderer and display modes remain in follow-up issue #3848.

issues.title: ToolFileInteractionContext ownership
issues.sourceOfTruth: RunContext owns run facts; ToolRunContext and ToolCallContext separate run-owned and call-owned tool facts
acceptance: Run-owned facts stay in RunContext/ToolRunContext.
Per-call facts stay in ToolCallContext.
Ownerless context bags and pass-through accessors are removed or justified by an ownership boundary.
The active tool-call context follows async execution scope rather than process-global mutable state.
issues.partialDelivery: PR #3847 removes process-global context stack lifetime and moves runtime-host fallback ownership to the tools layer. Full reader separation remains in follow-up issue #3849.

focusedFollowUps.title: CLI follow-up: validate texra run packaged runtime path
acceptance: Build and execute the package-local texra binary rather than only TypeScript entry points.

focusedFollowUps.title: CLI follow-up: implement ask approval prompts and matrix validation
focusedFollowUps.sourceOfTruth: packages/cli/src/runtime/approvalAdapter.ts maps CLI approval policy to decisions; shared coordinators own request identity and lifecycle
acceptance: Implement interactive ask prompts for CLI approval requests without duplicating shared coordinator lifecycle logic.
In non-TTY or headless mode, ask fails closed with a clear message instead of waiting forever.
Validate the approval matrix for bash, edit, plan, proposal, retry, and external inquiry paths.
Map denied or failed-closed approval outcomes to CliExitCode.ApprovalDenied at the CLI boundary.
Keep request identity and lifecycle in shared coordinators; the CLI adapter owns only policy-to-decision mapping and terminal prompting.
Keep tool-specific handlers free of CLI flag parsing and policy interpretation.

Add focused validation for grouped logging and sink behavior.
